messages:
Anya: Heads-up: Product wants a 'cost provenance' column in the cost dashboard so each per-route saving shows whether it came from prefix cache, prefetch, or routing demux. How feasible?
Mike: Doable but we need attribution surfaced in telemetry. Right now we log cache_hit=true and model_sku, but we don't record which policy (sticky routing / fallback / prefetch) caused the hit.
Sophia: Can we approximate by order-of-ops? e.g. if route sticky=true && cached_kv_used then attribute to routing. Multi-model chains will still be messy though. :thinking_face: 
Omar: Big concern: adding attribution tags per request will increase cardinality and ingestion costs. We should consider sampling or batch-level annotations.
Anya: Product ok with deterministic low sample (1%) plus an expand-to-trace UX for full detail. They want a primary attribution + confidence. A sparkline for sampled confidence would be ideal.
Mike: Prototype telemetry config I sketched:
```
cost_provenance: {
  enabled: true,
  sample_rate: 0.01,
  tags: ["routing_policy","cache_shard","prefetch_phase"]
}
```
Sophia: UX note: attribution needs clear semantics — e.g., prefetch should only count if it actually served tokens. Otherwise it inflates "savings".
infra-bot: Reminder: introducing these fields requires telemetry schema v2. This will be a forward-only change; historical backfill not supported.
Lina: UX proposal: show primary attribution column (enum) with a "Why" flyout that shows a short chain of events and a link to the sampled raw trace. Also add a filter to view only routing-attributed savings.
Omar: Implementation plan: start with low-cardinality enum: attribution={none, routing, cache, prefetch, fallback}. Keep per-request metadata minimal; push details to sampled traces. This keeps cost of telemetry bounded.
Anya: Action items: Omar + Mike to draft telemetry proto + sampling plan; Lina + Sophia to mock the dashboard flyout; Product is fine with 1% to start. @devex FYI. :thumbsup:
